measurements.takenOn: main, before this branch: the hall layout, no memory of place
measurements.note: The starting map of main: one hall, six internal pillars and the dig pocket. This block keeps its hash because it names a commit on `main`, which survives rebase and squash and still resolves; the 'after' block below names the tree in prose instead, because an in-branch hash does not (Issue #106 is the general form).

The dungeon on its own, with CanYield untouched. This is the measurement Issue #117 asks for: did the new layout raise how often a step stalls. It did, by half again, which is what authorised fixing #119 inside this task.
measurements.caveat: Taken on an intermediate layout of this branch, not on the one that shipped: the chambers were the same, the doorways were narrower. It is kept because it is the measurement the decision to fix #119 was made on, and because a later, wider layout cannot be used to justify a fix that was needed by the narrow one.

measurements.takenOn: the head of this branch after the review round: dungeon, CanYield fix, memory of place, the re-authored prepared plan and the R4 repeat fix
measurements.note: No yield order goes to a creature that cannot take the step, and stalled steps are back inside the range the hall produced.
measurements.supersedes: An earlier 'after' block, taken when the dungeon and the CanYield fix landed but before memory of place and before the R4 repeat fix. It read 5850-9500 stalled steps and was quoted by contract 4.5 as 5002-9500; both were stale by the time the branch was reviewed.
